locator: I q.2 a.3 ad 2: cum natura propter determinatum finem operetur ex directione alicuius superioris agentis, necesse est ea quae a natura fiunt, etiam in Deum reducere, sicut in primam causam ... oportet autem omnia mobilia et deficere possibilia reduci in aliquod primum principium immobile
interpretation: Literal reading of ad 2: what nature does for a determinate end, under a higher agent's direction, is reduced to God as first cause, and whatever is movable and defectible to a first immovable principle (sicut ostensum est: the earlier ways). It does not state that this first cause itself directs each natural body to the same end, nor that it is knowing and intelligent; it only bears on the open bridge STMT-NATURAL-DIRECTION-REDUCED-TO-IMMOBILE-FIRST (supports relation). Not used by any result.
